SELECT cls,
  CASE WHEN fish_date_doy BETWEEN 150 AND 179 THEN '150-179'
       WHEN fish_date_doy BETWEEN 120 AND 149 THEN '120-149' END AS bucket,
  COUNT(*) AS n_trips, SUM(yt) AS yt, SUM(anglers) AS anglers,
  ROUND(SUM(yt)::DOUBLE/NULLIF(SUM(anglers),0),4) AS share_per_angler
FROM trips
WHERE fish_date_season=2 AND fish_date_doy BETWEEN 120 AND 179
  AND cls IN ('three_quarter','overnight','day_1_5')
GROUP BY 1,2
ORDER BY 2,1

SELECT index_id, avail_doy, value FROM climate
WHERE index_id='oni' AND avail_season=2
ORDER BY avail_doy DESC LIMIT 5

SELECT boat, COUNT(*) n, SUM(yt) yt, SUM(anglers) anglers, ROUND(SUM(yt)::DOUBLE/NULLIF(SUM(anglers),0),4) AS ypa
FROM trips
WHERE fish_date_season=2 AND fish_date_doy BETWEEN 138 AND 152 AND cls='three_quarter'
GROUP BY boat ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 10

# Season 2 planning notes (written day 1, from season 1 full-season data)

## Bottom line
Yellowtail are essentially a longer-trip-only game. Half-day AM/PM and twilight trips are a
waste of money almost all season:
- hd_am share ≈0.009, hd_pm ≈0.010, hd_twilight ≈0.0, pooled over the whole season.
- Even in their best months (Apr-May) hd_am/hd_pm only hit ~0.03-0.06 share, and by June they're
  basically 0 through November.
=> Do not book HD_AM / HD_PM / TWILIGHT for yellowtail. Only use them if PTO/budget is otherwise idle
and another species matters (it doesn't for scoring), i.e. basically never.

The three classes that matter: THREE_QUARTER ($150), OVERNIGHT ($400), DAY_1_5 ($550).
Season-pooled share: three_quarter 0.242, overnight 0.419, day_1_5 0.457 (day_1_5/overnight also
included "multi_day" in raw class list but multi_day itself is NEVER offered/bookable - ignore it).
Season-pooled share-per-dollar: three_quarter 0.00161 > overnight 0.00105 > day_1_5 0.00083.
So three_quarter is the efficient default, but overnight/day_1_5 raise the ceiling on good windows.

## Seasonal timing (doy = day of year, buckets of 30 days, season 1 data)
Strong bimodal pattern - spring peak, summer trough, fall rebound:
- doy 90-119 (~April): three_quarter 0.51, overnight 1.48(!), day_1_5 2.21(n=7, thin)
- doy 120-149 (~May):  three_quarter 0.54, overnight 0.29, day_1_5 0.46(n=7, thin)
- doy 150-179 (~June): three_quarter 0.42, overnight 0.66, day_1_5 0.18
- doy 180-209 (~July):  three_quarter 0.06, overnight 0.01, day_1_5 0.01   <- TROUGH starts
- doy 210-239 (~Aug):   three_quarter 0.04, overnight 0.26, day_1_5 0.03
- doy 240-269 (~late Aug/Sep): three_quarter 0.02, overnight 0.06, day_1_5 0.04   <- TROUGH bottom
- doy 270-299 (~late Sep/Oct): three_quarter 0.30, overnight 0.64, day_1_5 2.16(n=69, solid)  <- FALL RUN
- doy 300-329 (~Nov):   three_quarter 0.07, overnight 0.20, day_1_5 2.01(n=5, thin)
- doy 330+ (~Dec):      basically 0 everywhere.

Read: April (doy90-119) and the Sep27-Oct26 window (doy270-299) are the two strongest windows across
every class, especially day_1_5 and overnight. July through most of September (doy180-269) is a real
trough - avoid committing PTO/budget there unless real-time signals (forecast, recent counts, fishdope
text) say otherwise. Caveat: several of the best numbers come from small n (7-15 trips) - trust the
live briefing's "recent counts" over these historical averages when they disagree, especially for
day_1_5 in April/Nov.

## Boats that stood out (n>=8 trips, overnight+day_1_5 pooled, season 1)
Prefer these when `ctx.scheduled_boats` lists them, over the naive `pick_boat` default:
Pacific Voyager (Seaforth, share 1.57), Cortez (Seaforth, 1.42), Ranger 85 (H&M, 1.28, n=29 - solid
sample), Top Gun 80 (H&M, 1.20), Constitution (H&M, 0.99), Grande (Point Loma, 0.83), Tomahawk
(Seaforth, 0.78, n=28 - solid), Mustang (H&M, 0.65, n=41 - solid sample). Ranger 85, Tomahawk and
Mustang have the most trips behind them so weight those most.

## Signals checked that did NOT help (season 1)
Daily fishdope numeric fields (migrated, yt_local, yt_all, wt_all) barely correlated with same-day
realized share across three_quarter/overnight/day_1_5 (all |corr| < 0.05, overlap sample was small).
Don't lean on the numeric fishdope columns alone - if using fishdope, read the narrative `text` field
directly at the nightly briefing rather than trusting the numeric summary fields.

## Season 2 ONI/water-temp tracking (updated each planning turn)
- doy9 -1.57 -> doy40 -1.48 -> doy71 -1.29 -> doy99 -1.06 -> doy130 -0.85. Steady, roughly linear
  recovery out of deep La Nina, ~+0.7 over 130 days (~+0.15/month). If the pace holds, ONI could be
  in the -0.1 to -0.3 range by doy270 (the fall-run window) - still negative/La-Nina-ish but much
  closer to neutral than the season opened. Re-check at the next planning turn; don't assume the
  linear pace continues, but so far it hasn't stalled or reversed once since day 1.
- Pier wtmp_c ran ~0.9-1.6C colder than season-1's matched-doy readings through the winter/spring
  (checked doy1-32 and doy78-91). Have not rechecked the gap since doy91 - do that next time water
  temp becomes decision-relevant (i.e. as the fall window approaches, ~doy255-260).

## Season 2 realized catch by class, by doy bucket (live data, updated day 152)
- doy1-91 (winter+early spring): essentially all zero across every class (confirmed day 60 and day 91
  planning turns). One early signal: fishdope text doy85 "1st fish of the season" (2 yt, HD_PM, one
  boat) - thin, didn't repeat immediately.
- doy91-120ish (spring bite, mostly on ONE boat): San Diego (3Q) carried the whole spring - see journal
  d98-d150 for the full chase. Net: six 3Q bookings d99-d150 area, one big spike (d106, 23/45=0.51),
  rest mostly zero/small, season score currently 0.6281 from this. Fleet-pooled 3Q only reached
  ~0.06-0.10/angler through this period - San Diego was a real, if noisy, single-boat edge, not a
  fleet-wide bite.
- doy120-149 (May, live S2 pooled, n=70/27/13 trips): three_quarter 0.1578, overnight 0.1285,
  day_1_5 0.0203. This is real and non-trivial (much better than winter dead-zero) but still well
  below S1's May numbers (0.54/0.29/0.46) - a "warm, cold-year" muted version of the S1 pattern, not
  absent, not equal.
- doy150-152 (first 3 days of the June bucket, as of day 152 - THIN, only 8 three_quarter trips
  fleet-wide): yt=1/264 anglers, share 0.0038. Crashed hard and fast right at the doy150 mark. San
  Diego itself: 10 trips in the trailing 15 days (doy138-152) pooled 0.396 ypa (137 yt/346 anglers,
  driven by strong prints in the 138-149 stretch), but the two most recent bookings (d148, d150) were
  0.0 and 0.016 - i.e. the boat's own signal is now cooling in exactly the days that pushed the
  30-day pool into the "150-179" bucket. Read: the S1 pattern was June still decent (0.42) with the
  trough starting ~doy180; S2's trough may be starting ~3-4 weeks EARLIER, right at doy150, following
  a weaker spring bite overall. One 3-day bucket is not proof - confirm over the next 1-2 weeks before
  concluding the trough has arrived, but do NOT keep chasing San Diego's May average once real-time
  prints go quiet, the same discipline that correctly called the d106-d107 round-trip in April.
- Other boats worth noting in the May stretch: Mission Belle (3Q, 0.2207 ypa, n=7, doy138-152),
  Malihini (3Q, 0.1447, n=11) - both real fleet participants, not just San Diego. If San Diego goes
  fully quiet, check these two before assuming the whole fleet is dead.

## Status as of day 152 planning turn (season score 0.6281, rank 6/34 live agents; budget $800/2000,
PTO 8/10)
- PTO already committed for S02 d158 and d159 (2 weekday days) - decided on a prior nightly tick per
  journal (d144-145) on the strength of San Diego's then-0.52 ypa pooled signal, but the actual
  boat/class for that trip was NOT locked in notes - check the d158/159 briefings carefully: if the
  signal has cooled further (per the doy150-152 crash above), consider using a CHEAP class
  (three_quarter or even skipping if truly nothing bookable) on those committed dates rather than
  stretching to overnight/day_1_5 just because PTO is already sunk - PTO already spent is a sunk cost,
  don't let it force a bigger bet than the live data supports.
- We are rank 6 of 34, solidly mid-pack among agents that are actually fishing (many bot strategies
  like B_SAT/B_TEMP/B_BIG are still at 0). calendarist (0.7045) and follower (0.6681) lead - both also
  labeled "no strategy yet" so their edge came from nightly judgment calls too, not code. Nothing here
  suggests a fundamentally different approach is needed, just continued discipline plus not missing the
  fall window.
- Budget pacing: $1200 spent of $2000 (60%) by day 152 (~50% of the Apr-Nov season by calendar) - a bit
  ahead of pure 50/50 pacing but not alarmingly so, and PTO is barely touched (2/10 committed, 0 used
  yet since twilight/weekend trips avoided PTO). This leaves plenty of room ($800, 8 PTO) for the fall
  run - don't feel forced to hold back further, but also don't spend the $800 down chasing three_quarter
  noise through a trough if the doy150-152 crash is real and sustained.

## Concrete plan for the rest of the season (day 152 onward)
1. Treat doy150-270ish as the likely trough (per both S1's historical pattern and S2's own just-started
   crash) - hold most of the remaining $800/8 PTO through this stretch. Keep using cheap $150
   three_quarter "prober" bookings only on days that are free of PTO (weekends/holidays) AND have a
   live boat-specific edge (recheck San Diego, Mission Belle, Malihini pooled ypa each tick) - exactly
   the discipline that has worked all season. Don't commit new weekday PTO into this stretch without a
   real, repeating (2+ trip) signal.
2. Start watching ~doy255-260 (14 days before the fall-run window opens at doy270) for: (a) ONI
   continuing its recovery pace (was -0.85 at doy130 - check the latest value then), (b) pier wtmp_c
   closing further vs season-1's matched-doy fall readings, (c) any early fishdope text mentioning
   yellowtail returning, (d) fleet-pooled 3Q/overnight/day_1_5 ticking up off the trough floor.
3. If those fall-window signals look reasonable (ONI continuing to climb, even one or two real prints),
   commit weekday PTO into doy270-299 more aggressively than April's slow ramp - April cost us most of
   a window waiting for confirmation before the d106 spike; the fall window has the strongest, most
   reliable S1 sample (day_1_5 2.16 over n=69) and we now have real S2 in-season evidence (spring bite
   was muted but real, ONI recovering) that this season is not a total washout, just a delayed/damped
   one. Named boats to prioritize if scheduled: Pacific Voyager, Cortez, Ranger 85, Top Gun 80,
   Constitution, Tomahawk, Mustang (S1 standouts) plus San Diego, Mission Belle, Malihini (S2 spring
   standouts on three_quarter).
4. Sizing: with $800/8 PTO left and the fall window being the main remaining opportunity, a reasonable
   target is 1-2 day_1_5 trips ($550 each) or a day_1_5 + overnight combo, funded mostly from the fall
   window, plus continued opportunistic $150 three_quarter probes on PTO-free days throughout. Don't
   spend it all on three_quarter probes through the trough - keep at least ~$550-700 and 4+ PTO days
   in reserve heading into doy255.
5. strategy.py remains a no-op - manual nightly signal-chasing (chase/drop a boat's live edge, treat a
   single spike as noise until confirmed, round-trip detection) has clearly outperformed any naive
   calendar/threshold rule so far (rank 6 vs 8+ bot strategies stuck at 0) and there's still no simple
   rule that would replicate the judgment calls made all season (e.g. distinguishing San Diego's d106
   spike from its d144-149 sustained run). Keep it a no-op unless nightly turns start getting missed.

## Open questions for next planning turn (as of day 152)
- Is the doy150-152 three_quarter crash (0.0038 ypa, n=8) a real, sustained trough onset, or just 3
  noisy days? Recheck the 150-179 bucket with more data next time (should have 2-4 weeks more by then).
- Did San Diego, Mission Belle, or Malihini keep producing at all through late June, or go fully to
  zero like the S1 trough pattern? This determines whether ANY three_quarter probing is worth it before
  the fall window, or whether to just hold everything until doy255+.
- Latest ONI reading and pier wtmp_c gap vs season 1 - update the recovery-pace extrapolation
  (currently projecting roughly -0.1 to -0.3 ONI by doy270) with the newest data point.
- What was the d158/d159 PTO commitment actually for? Check upcoming briefings/results next turn to
  see what boat/class got booked on those dates and whether it paid off - that's a direct read on
  whether "commit PTO ahead of confirmation, on a strong-but-cooling boat signal" was the right call.
- Budget/PTO pace check at ~doy220 (next natural checkpoint): should still have most of the $800/8 PTO
  intact if the trough holds; if not, understand why before the fall window arrives.

---
(Earlier day-by-day planning-turn history: day 32 ONI/water-temp cold-open finding, day 60 confirmation
of no recovery + winter dead-zero, day 91 first fishdope yellowtail signal, day 121 San Diego chase
summary and 0.6117 season score - all superseded by the "Season 2 ONI/water-temp tracking" and
"Season 2 realized catch by class" sections above, which carry the full running history forward. Full
verbatim text of those earlier updates was trimmed here to keep the file readable; the substance is
preserved in the tracking sections.)
